items.meaning: DHCP 提供 BOOTP 所提供功能的超集
DHCP 消息格式基于 BOOTP 消息格式
BOOTP 中的 vendor extensions 字段在 DHCP 中更名为 options 字段
带有 DHCP message type 选项类型 1 的 DHCP 消息称为 DHCPDISCOVER 消息
DHCP 服务器收到的包含 DHCP message type (51) 选项的消息被假定由 DHCP 客户端发送
DHCP 服务器对 BOOTP 客户端的支持由本地系统管理员酌情决定
未配置支持 BOOTP 客户端的 DHCP 服务器收到来自 BOOTP 客户端的 BOOTREQUEST 时会静默丢弃该消息
items.constraint: 未配置支持 BOOTP 客户端时静默丢弃

items.meaning: 已配置支持 BOOTP 客户端的 DHCP 服务器可被配置提供静态地址、自动地址或两者
静态地址是系统管理员先前分配并存储在 DHCP 服务器可用数据库中的地址
自动地址是 DHCP 服务器从其未分配地址池中选择的地址
允许 DHCP 服务器返回自动地址的决定必须由系统管理员控制
items.constraint: 必须由系统管理员控制

items.meaning: BOOTP relay agents 原称 BOOTP forwarding agents
文档描述一种机制，使 DHCP 服务器能告知客户端没有可提供的 IP 地址
客户端不应自行生成 IP 地址
items.constraint: SHOULD NOT generate an IP address its own

items.meaning: DHCP 提供由站点管理员向网络设备提供 IP 地址及其他网络参数的方法
IPv4 地址自动配置可按子网或按节点禁用
items.constraint: may be disabled on a per-subnet or per-node basis

items.meaning: 节点可给自己分配 IP 地址并与本地链路上的其他节点完全连通
文档定义一个新的 DHCP 选项，由 DHCP 服务器传给 DHCP 客户端
RFC 2132 允许 DHCP 服务器指定各种名称服务的配置信息并传给 DHCP 客户端
无法通过 DHCP 指定搜索顺序
文档目的是允许 DHCP 服务器指定 DHCP 客户端使用的搜索顺序
DHCP 客户端是使用 DHCP 获取网络地址等配置参数的 Internet 主机
DHCP 服务器是向 DHCP 客户端返回配置参数的 Internet 主机
该选项的代码为 117，最小长度为 2 字节
items.constraint: minimum length is 2 bytes

items.meaning: DHCP 服务器应按偏好顺序返回名称服务的 16 位网络字节序整数选项代码
items.constraint: SHOULD return in preferred order; 16-bit network byte order; earlier in list more preferred

items.meaning: DHCP 提供在 TCP/IP 网络上向主机传递配置信息的框架
配置参数和其他控制信息携带在存储在 DHCP 消息 options 字段中的标记数据项里
这些数据项本身也称为 options
DHCP 协议消息由 DHCP Message Type 选项（选项代码 51）标识
items.constraint: option code 51

items.meaning: 每种消息类型由 DHCP Message Type 选项携带的数据值定义
DHCP 客户端用来可选地标识其所代表的用户或应用类型/类别的选项。
items.constraint: This option should be configurable by a user.

items.meaning: 使用 DHCP 获取网络地址等配置参数的 Internet 主机。
包含至少一个 IP 地址并与 DHCP 客户端关联或绑定的配置参数集合，由 DHCP 服务器管理。
允许 DHCP 客户端指定在其上分配地址的子网的新 DHCP 选项。
items.constraint: This option takes precedence over the methods that the DHCP server uses to determine the subnet on which to select an address.

items.meaning: DHCP 服务器确定请求来源的子网，并在来源子网或同一网段子网上选择地址。
DHCP 包头部中的 giaddr 字段的子网地址可用于确定请求来源的子网；若该字段为零，则使用本地接口的子网地址。
由 DHCP 中继代理在向 DHCP 服务器转发客户端发起的 DHCP 包时插入的新 DHCP 选项。
在向 DHCP 服务器转发客户端发起的 DHCP 包时插入 Relay Agent Information 选项的实体。
Relay Agent Information 选项包含一个或多个子选项，用于传递中继代理已知的信息。
在服务器到客户端的响应中向中继代理原样回显该选项，随后中继代理在向客户端转发响应前移除该选项。
一种算法负载均衡方法，使多个协作服务器无需交换初始配置之外的信息即可决定由哪台服务器服务客户端。
当多台 DHCP 服务器可服务 DHCP 客户端时，服务器选择基于对客户端 Media Access Control（MAC）地址进行哈希。
该协议最初被设计用于支持 DHCP Failover Protocol 的一项特定负载均衡优化。
具有适当授权的新接入主机可由经过认证的 DHCP 服务器自动配置。
网络管理员可能希望提供 DHCP 消息来源和内容的认证。
A unicast FORCERENEW message is introduced to force the client to the RENEW state.
The DHCP server sends a unicast FORCERENEW message to the client.
Upon receipt of the unicast FORCERENEW message, the client changes to the RENEW state and tries to renew its lease according to normal DHCP procedures.
If the server wants to assign a new IP address to the client, it replies to the DHCP REQUEST with a DHCP NAK.
If the FORCERENEW message is lost, the DHCP server should retransmit it using an exponential backoff algorithm.
items.constraint: should retransmit using an exponential backoff algorithm

items.meaning: Receipt of a multicast FORCERENEW message by the client should be silently discarded.
items.constraint: should be silently discarded

items.meaning: A new sub-option is proposed for the DHCP Relay Agent Information Option.
The sub-option describes the device class to which a cable modem belongs.
The cable modem signals device class information to the Relay Agent using DOCSIS signaling, and the Relay Agent forwards it to the DHCP Server.
The relay agent passes the Device Class value unchanged to the DHCP server.
items.constraint: MUST pass unchanged

items.meaning: DOCSIS defines the Device Class as a 32-bit field where individual bits represent individual attributes of the CM.
Defines a DHCP-for-IPv4 option containing a list of domain names or IPv4 addresses mapped to SIP outbound proxy servers.
A SIP server in this document must be an outbound proxy server.
items.constraint: MUST be an outbound proxy server

items.meaning: The DHCP option allows SIP clients to locate a local SIP server used for all outbound SIP requests, called an outbound proxy server.
The SIP server DHCP option carries a 32-bit IPv4 address or preferably a DNS fully-qualified domain name used by the SIP client to locate a SIP server.
A new DHCP option is passed from the DHCP Server to the DHCP Client to configure a list of static routes in the client.
Each routing table entry includes a subnet mask, and the network destinations are classless.
This option obsoletes the Static Route option (option 33) defined in RFC 2132.
The host routing table can be maintained using the DHCP Router option defined in RFC 2132.
The DHCP protocol and RFC 2132 options only provide a mechanism for installing a default route or a table of classful routes.
Classful routing is no longer in common use, so the DHCP Static Route option is no longer useful.
Defines a DHCP option used to configure various devices deployed within CableLabs architectures.
The option content is used to configure one class of CableLabs client device: a PacketCable Media Terminal Adapter (MTA).
The option content will be extended as future CableLabs client devices are developed.
DHCP option code 80 name, defined in an expired Internet-Draft, contact Charlie Perkins, reason to recover never published as standard and not in general use.
items.constraint: Listed as unused and to be returned to IANA for reassignment to future DHCP options.

items.meaning: DHCP option codes 83 and 84 name, defined in an early draft of RFC 3046, reason to recover not defined in RFC 3046 as published.
items.constraint: Listed as unused and to be returned to IANA for reassignment to future DHCP options.

items.meaning: DHCP option code 89 name, defined in an expired Internet-Draft, contact Ralph Droms who agrees the option code should be reassigned, reason to recover never published as standard and not in general use.
items.constraint: Listed as unused and to be returned to IANA for reassignment to future DHCP options.

items.meaning: Identifiers contained in two new DHCP options to remove ambiguity when a DHCP client represents multiple vendors.
DHCP option that allows a client to indicate its vendor type; the vendor identified by option 60 defines the interpretation of option 43.
DHCP option used by the DHCP client and server to exchange vendor-specific information.
DHCP Unique Identifier specified in DHCPv6; conforming DHCPv4 client implementations use it to identify themselves.
items.constraint: DHCPv4 client implementations that conform to this specification use a DUID as specified in DHCPv6.

items.meaning: DHCPv4 option in which the DUID is encapsulated.
DNS resource record related to the client's address assignment; the DHCPv4 option can convey responsibility for updating it.

Information including country, administrative units such as states, provinces, and cities, street addresses, postal community names, and building information, with the option allowing multiple renditions of the same address in different scripts and languages.
Document obsoleted by RFC 4776; RFC 4776 corrects an error in the assignment of the numeric value of the DHCPv6 option-code in RFC 4676.
items.constraint: RFC 4776 obsoletes RFC 4676.

items.meaning: DHCPv6 option code whose numeric value was assigned with an error in RFC 4676 and corrected by RFC 4776.
POSIX 1003.1 timezone strings are one common way to communicate timezone information.
Timezone database names are one common way to communicate timezone information.
This memo specifies DHCP options for each of the two timezone communication methods.
The DHCPv4 time offset option is deprecated.
items.constraint: deprecated

items.meaning: This memo defines a new suboption of the DHCP relay agent information option.
The new suboption is defined under the DHCP relay agent information option.
The DHCP relay can specify flags for the forwarded packet.
A flag indicates whether the DHCP relay received the packet via unicast or broadcast.
The DHCP server may use this information to better serve clients based on whether their request was originally broadcast or unicast.
This memo defines a DHCPv4 VSS option.
This memo defines a DHCPv6 VSS option.
This memo defines DHCPv4 VSS and VSS-Control sub-options.
The DHCPv4 VSS and VSS-Control sub-options are carried in the DHCPv4 Relay Agent Information option.
The VSS options are intended for use by DHCP clients, relay agents, and proxy clients.
For the DHCPv4 option and Relay Agent Information sub-options, this memo documents and extends existing usage as per RFC 3942.
This memo updates RFC 3046 regarding details relating to the copying of sub-options.
DHCP FORCERENEW allows reconfiguration of a single host by forcing the DHCP client into a Renew state on a trigger from the DHCP server.
In the Forcerenew Nonce Authentication protocol, the server sends a nonce to the client in the initial DHCP ACK for subsequent validation of a FORCERENEW message.
The initial DHCP ACK carries the nonce used for subsequent validation of a FORCERENEW message.
This document updates RFC 3203.
This document updates RFC 2131 Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol.
This document addresses issues arising from RFC 2131's specification that the server MUST NOT return the client identifier option to the client.
items.constraint: server MUST NOT return it to the client

items.meaning: This document defines an extension to the DHCP protocols that allows a relay agent to use any available source port for upstream communications.
A relay agent may use any available source port for upstream communications.
A DHCP option can be used to statelessly route responses back to the appropriate source port on downstream communications.
This document describes a DHCPv4 and DHCPv6 option to inform clients that they are behind a captive portal enforcement device and need to satisfy Captive Portal conditions to get Internet access.
A Router Advertisement option informs clients that they are behind a captive portal enforcement device and need to satisfy Captive Portal conditions to get Internet access.
This document replaces RFC 7710, which used DHCP code point 160.
This document specifies DHCP code point 114 due to a conflict.
This document also updates RFC 3679.
This document specifies a DHCPv4 option to indicate that a host supports an IPv6-only mode and is willing to forgo obtaining an IPv4 address if the network provides IPv6 connectivity.

This document updates RFC 2563 to specify DHCPv4 server behavior when the server receives a DHCPDISCOVER not containing the Auto-Configure option but containing the new option defined in this document.
When a DHCPDISCOVER does not contain the Auto-Configure option but contains the new option defined in this document, RFC 2563 is updated to specify DHCPv4 server behavior.
The absence of the Auto-Configure option together with the presence of the new option affects specified DHCPv4 server behavior.
This document specifies new DHCP options to discover encrypted DNS resolvers such as DNS over HTTPS, DNS over TLS, and DNS over QUIC.
This document specifies new IPv6 Router Advertisement options to discover encrypted DNS resolvers.
Encrypted DNS resolvers can include DNS over HTTPS, DNS over TLS, and DNS over QUIC.
A host can learn an Authentication Domain Name together with a list of IP addresses and a set of service parameters to reach encrypted DNS resolvers.
An IP/UDP bootstrap protocol that allows a diskless client machine to discover its own IP address, the address of a server host, and the name of a file to be loaded into memory and executed.
The bootstrap operation can be thought of as consisting of two phases; this RFC describes the first phase.
The file transfer will typically use the TFTP protocol.
A single packet exchange is performed.
items.constraint: Timeouts are used to retransmit until a reply is received.

items.meaning: An opcode field exists with two values.
The client broadcasts a bootrequest packet.
The server answers with a bootreply packet.
The bootrequest contains the client's hardware address and its IP address, if known.
The request can optionally contain the name of the server the client wishes to respond.
The function of dealing with name/domain services is pushed off to the BOOTP server.
The request can optionally contain the 'generic' filename to be booted.
When the server sends the bootreply, it replaces the filename field with the fully qualified path name of the appropriate boot file.
The server may consult its own database correlating the client's address and filename request with a particular boot file.
Clients in networks that use services provided by DHCPv4 over DHCPv6 in a Relay Agent.
Specifies the use of DHCPv4 over DHCPv6 in the client only.
Can implement the DHCPv4-over-DHCPv6 encapsulation and decapsulation of DHCPv4 messages in DHCPv6 messages on behalf of a DHCPv4 client.
Encapsulation and decapsulation mechanism for carrying DHCPv4 messages in DHCPv6 messages.
Protocol whose messages are encapsulated and decapsulated in DHCPv6 messages.
Protocol in whose messages DHCPv4 messages are encapsulated and decapsulated.
